title: Бессонная ночь и приход хозяйки  (A Sleepless Night and the Owner's Arrival)

segments.t: Before the staff meeting in the lobby, Katya apologizes to Denis and says she could not sleep all night, while Denis hides the reason he barely slept—until owner Eleonora Andreevna walks in. Listen to the scene.
Я тоже всю ночь не спал.
О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
А вот и владелица нашего отеля.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Hi, Denis.' Katya evenly speaks this casual greeting without hesitation using "privet" ("hi") — the everyday informal hello used between friends and close coworkers.
'Hi, Katya.' Denis smoothly speaks this casual greeting toward Katya using "privet" ("hi") — the everyday informal hello used between friends and close coworkers.
'You were upset because of yesterday.' Katya chimes in briskly with a nod, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
'No, everything is fine.' Denis opens up sharply before Katya and uses "normalno" ("fine, OK") to carry the main weight of the thought.
'Forgive me, please.' Katya lightly extends this personal apology for Denis using "prosti" ("forgive me") — the close, informal way to say "forgive me" or "I'm sorry" to someone dear.
'I was very worried all night.' Katya chimes in bluntly without any doubt, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'I did not sleep at all today.' Katya speaks up firmly in the exchange and reaches for the Russian word "segodnya" ("today") right at the heart of the line.
Я тоже всю ночь не спал.
'I did not sleep all night either.' Mentioning the night in front of Katya, Denis puts the emphasis on "noch" ("night") in the middle of the talk.
'I tossed and turned all night long.' Mentioning the night without a pause, Denis sets the direction for the rest of the talk with Katya.

'It is clear why you did not get enough sleep.' Katya lightly directs this acknowledgment as they meet using "ponyatno" ("understood") — a single word meaning "clear, got it", showing the point has landed.
О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
'Report any problems to me immediately.' Bringing up the problem at once, Eleonora leans on "problemakh" ("problem", a form of "problema") to give the remark its edge.
А вот и владелица нашего отеля.
'And here is the owner of our hotel.' Eleonora cuts in lightly watching Katya, watching Katya's face to see how the news lands.
'I did not come here to get acquainted.' Eleonora fires back briskly on the spot and lands on "znakomitsya" ("get acquainted") as the key everyday word here.
Я тоже всю ночь не спал.
О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
А вот и владелица нашего отеля.
And that introduces hotel owner Eleonora Andreevna. See you next time!

lines.fragment: А вот и замечательная владелица нашего отеля
